description: The controlled vocabulary a workflow declares itself into. Declared, never inferred: guessing a category from the workflow name silently mis-files runs, and a mis-filed run is compared against work it never did. A workflow declares exactly one category - the category of the work its grade is mostly about - and an unrecognised id is rejected rather than stored.
cohort_note: Category cohorts compare different workflows doing similar work, so cost and speed are only admitted once normalised per work unit. `other` never forms a cohort: it is the escape hatch for work that fits nothing here, which by definition has no peers.

categories.label: Document generation
categories.definition: Produces a substantial document from a brief and source material - a CV, a report, a proposal, a specification, a set of templates.

categories.label: Correspondence
categories.definition: Drafts messages addressed to a specific counterparty - customer replies, outcome emails, follow-ups. Distinct from document generation because the audience is a person in a thread, not a reader of a deliverable.

categories.label: Classification and routing
categories.definition: Assigns incoming items to categories, severities, owners or queues against a stated rubric.

categories.label: Data extraction
categories.definition: Pulls structured data out of unstructured or semi-structured sources into a defined shape.

categories.label: Summarisation
categories.definition: Condenses existing material without adding new claims - meeting notes, document digests, thread recaps.

categories.label: Research and analysis
categories.definition: Gathers and reasons over information to reach a conclusion or recommendation the inputs do not state directly.

categories.label: Code generation
categories.definition: Writes, modifies or reviews source code, tests or configuration.

categories.label: Other
categories.definition: Work that fits none of the above. Runs here are scored and reported normally but never form a category cohort.
